newsitem.title: USA: Rains bring some relief to dry Montana fields.
newsitem.headline: Rains bring some relief to dry Montana fields.

text.p: Scattered rains brought some relief to parched Montana fields but dry conditions prevailed across much of the state, delaying winter wheat seeding, the Montana Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly report.
Winter wheat was three percent seeded as of Sunday but most farmers were waiting for additional moisture.
Topsoil moisture was rated 49 percent very short, 42 percent short, nine percent adequate and nil surplus.
Spring wheat was 88 percent harvested, compared with 83 percent last year and 62 percent for the five-year average.
Barley was 85 percent harvested, against 62 percent last year and average of 67 percent.
The oat harvest was also ahead of average with 87 percent harvested as of Sunday, compared with 63 last year and the five-year average of 65 percent.
Pasture and range conditions were rated nine percent very poor, 32 percent poor, 35 percent fair, 22 percent good and two percent excellent.
